editorial.headline: Chemical Wholesale Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration for it.
editorial.body:
In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA today. That conclusion sits beside a very different national position: the activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The distinction matters because national openness does not override Bali’s stated, island-wide rule for PMA registration. For this activity, the Bali result is recorded as **Blocked (risk class)**.

The activity itself is wholesale trade in a broad range of non-hazardous basic or industrial chemical materials and goods. Its stated scope includes printer ink, essential oils, industrial gases—including hydrogen—chemical adhesives, dyes, synthetic resins, methanol, paraffin, flavourings and fragrances, soda, industrial salt, acids and sulphur. It is, in other words, a wholesale commercial category for supplying chemical inputs and related goods, while expressly excluding hazardous materials. The breadth of that list should not be mistaken for a licence to extend beyond the stated boundary: the record defines the category through non-hazardous chemical materials and goods.

The national record opens the activity to businesses operating at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. It also identifies the national PMA position through Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For an investor assessing the national framework alone, the message is straightforward: there is no foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The scale listing is equally broad, covering the full range from micro to large enterprises.

Bali changes the practical answer for PMA registration. The record states that, at the Besar scale, every scope is classified as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration on an island-wide, permanent basis. That is the decisive local fact: this is not a case of a reduced Bali foreign-ownership percentage or a conditional local partnership. It is a registration block for PMA in Bali, despite the 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling. Anyone considering this activity in Bali should therefore read the national openness and the provincial restriction together, with the Bali PMA block determining the local position.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not override Bali’s island-wide, permanent rule for PMA registration.
